title: ATAC-seq on nuclei from frozen Drosophila melanogaster embryo halves
author: Jenna Haines
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kj5cuq6
materials: Keep the slides, poker tool, and scalpel on dry ice to keep from melting. Shandon™ Straight Point Teasing Needles, Straight Point, Wooden Handle, 5.5 in. (14.0cm) Thermo Scientific Catalog #19010 Fisherbrand™ High Precision #10 Style Scalpel Blade Fisher Scientific Catalog #12-000-162
Crush using a plastic pestle upwards of 20 times vigorously. Pellet pestles Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #Z359947

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffers
steps.instruction: Make three buffers: (1) Lysis Buffer No Detergent – 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl₂; store at 4 °C and remake weekly. (2) Lysis Buffer Freezing Media – 10 mL of the No‑Detergent buffer plus 1 mL 50 % glycerol and 1 µL bromophenol‑blue dye. (3) Lysis Buffer + Spermine – 10 mL of the No‑Detergent buffer plus 0.15 mM spermine.

steps.title: Collect and age embryos
steps.instruction: Place several hundred adult Oregon R flies in a cage at 25 °C for 3 days, feeding standard molasses plates spread with yeast paste. Collect embryos for 2 h, then age them at 25 °C for 1 h 30 min to obtain embryos 2 h 00 min–3 h 30 min old.

steps.title: Dechorionate embryos
steps.instruction: Bleach embryos for 3 min in 30 %–50 % bleach solution to remove the chorion.

steps.title: Rinse and dry embryos
steps.instruction: Rinse embryos thoroughly with water and pat dry on a clean towel.

steps.title: Wash embryos with PBS‑Triton
steps.instruction: Rinse embryos with 1× PBS containing 0.5 % Triton X‑100.

steps.title: Transfer embryos to tube
steps.instruction: Brush embryos into a 1.5 mL tube containing 1× PBS + 0.5 % Triton, let them settle, then transfer a drop of embryos onto a slide for staging.

steps.title: Stage embryos
steps.instruction: Stage embryos to the desired developmental stage (commonly Stage 5).

steps.title: Place embryos in freezing media
steps.instruction: Transfer staged embryos into Eppendorf tubes containing Lysis Buffer Freezing Media.

steps.title: Prepare slide and freeze embryos
steps.instruction: Affix a grid pattern to the underside of a glass slide for contrast. Under a dissection microscope, space embryos evenly on the slide. Chill a cold block with dry ice, cool the scalpel and poker tools on dry ice, and wear gloves. Place the slide on the cold block (or directly on dry ice) for 2–5 min until embryos turn completely white (≈10 embryos per slide).

steps.title: Slice embryos and collect halves
steps.instruction: Using a dry‑ice‑chilled blade or scalpel, cut each embryo along the midline. Transfer each half immediately into a 1.5 mL tube containing 50 µL ATAC Lysis Buffer + Spermine. Use separate poker tools for anterior and posterior halves and wash each poker in 70 % ethanol between slices.

steps.title: Homogenize and adjust volume
steps.instruction: Homogenize the embryo halves. Rinse the pestle with 50 µL Lysis Buffer to recover all material, bringing the total volume to 100 µL.

steps.title: Vortex and spin down
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube at low speed, then spin briefly on a tabletop centrifuge to collect the lysate.

steps.title: Add IGEPAL to lysate
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 10 % IGEPAL CA‑630 drop‑wise (final concentration 0.1 %). Mix by flicking the tube and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei
steps.instruction: Spin the lysate in a microcentrifuge at 800 × g for 10 min at 4 °C. Carefully remove as much supernatant as possible to avoid nuclei loss.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei for transposition
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclear pellet in DNase‑ and RNase‑free water in a volume sufficient for the downstream transposition reaction.

steps.title: Prepare transposition mix on ice
steps.instruction: On ice, assemble the transposition reaction using the Nextera DNA Library Preparation Kit (Catalog #FC‑121‑1030).

steps.title: Perform tagmentation
steps.instruction: Add the resuspended nuclei to the transposition mix and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Purify tagmented DNA (bead cleanup)
steps.instruction: Add 1.25× volume of magnetic beads to the reaction, mix well, and let stand for 5 min. Place on a magnetic rack for 2 min. Wash the beads twice with 70 % ethanol. Remove ethanol, then resuspend the DNA in 20 µL H₂O. Let stand 1 min, place on magnet, and remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Store and quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Store purified DNA at –20 °C. Quantify DNA concentration using a Qubit fluorometer.

steps.title: Optional qPCR to set cycle number
steps.instruction: Set up a 15 µL qPCR reaction: 5 µL transposed DNA, 0.25 µL 25 µM Primer 1, 0.25 µL 25 µM Primer 2, 5 µL NEBNext 2× Master Mix, 3.9 µL H₂O, 0.09 µL 100× SYBR Green I dye. Run: 1 cycle 30 s at 98 °C; 20 cycles 10 s at 98 °C, 30 s at 63 °C, 1 min at 72 °C. Plot fluorescence versus cycle number and determine the cycle that reaches one‑third of the maximum signal; this is the additional number of cycles to use in the final PCR.

steps.title: Amplify transposed DNA (PCR)
steps.instruction: In a 50 µL PCR tube combine: 10 µL transposed DNA, 5 µL 25 µM Primer 1, 5 µL 25 µM Primer 2, 25 µL NEBNext 2× Master Mix, 5 µL PPC. Run the program: 72 °C 5 min; 98 °C 30 s; 98 °C 10 s; 63 °C 30 s; 72 °C 1 min; repeat steps 3–5 five times; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Run extra PCR cycles if needed
steps.instruction: Based on the qPCR result, perform additional cycles: 98 °C 30 s, 98 °C 10 s, 63 °C 30 s, 72 °C 1 min for the determined number of cycles, then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Validate libraries
steps.instruction: Quantify final libraries with Qubit HS DNA assay and assess fragment size distribution using a Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA assay.
